key_insight: NeuTNN-AV achieves competitive multimodal audio-visual classification using 4-bit weights, local learning, and far fewer synapses than leading spiking baselines.
engineering_relevance: Its comparison-and-addition inference offers a hardware-efficient approach for resource-constrained audio-visual sensing, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated.
method: Encode inputs temporally, with each input line spiking at most once.
Use neurons with multiple active dendritic segments and local reward-modulated STDP learning.
Store weights as 4-bit integers and perform inference using only comparisons and additions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 78.6% accuracy on CREMA-D with 2.34M synapses and 98.82% on UrbanSound8K-AV with 1.38M synapses, alongside 23–106× smaller weight memory than spiking baselines.
watch_item: Reported energy savings concern synaptic operations; end-to-end hardware efficiency, including input processing, remains to be established.
paper_title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
